question: For a basic rural roadside sign, combine Figure 2A-2 with Sections 2A.15 and 2A.16 to state the normal minimum mounting height and lateral offset.
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a basic roadside sign in a rural area, the normal minimum mounting height is 5 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement. The normal minimum lateral offset shown in Figure 2A-2 is 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, or 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder where the shoulder is wider than 6 feet. Where roadside features make these offsets impractical, Section 2A.16 permits a reduced lateral offset of as little as 2 feet on certain roads. Standards (mandatory): - "In rural areas, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 5 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - For contrast, in business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian movements are likely, "the minimum height … of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 7 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." Guidance (recommended): - The figure-related guidance notes that "Lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet measured from the edge of the shoulder, or 12 feet measured from the edge of the traveled way," and refers the reader to Section 2A.16 for lower minimums that may be used where lateral offset space is limited. Options (permitted): - "On conventional, low-volume rural, and special-purpose roads in areas where it is impractical to locate a sign with the lateral offset prescribed by this Section because of roadside features such as terrain or vegetation, a lateral offset of at least 2 feet may be used." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-2, drawings A and B ("Roadside sign in rural area"), shows a 5 ft MIN. height with a 12 ft MIN. lateral offset from the edge of the traveled way, or a 6 ft MIN. offset from the edge of a shoulder wider than 6 feet. - [Image 2] The full-page view of Figure 2A-2 confirms the same 5 ft MIN. height and 12 ft/6 ft MIN. lateral offsets for rural roadside signs, with a note directing readers to Section 2A.16 for reduced offsets. - [Image 4] Section 2A.15/2A.16 text confirms mounting height provisions and introduces the Lateral Offset standards, including the note that Figure 2A-2 illustrates the mounting height requirements. - [Image 5] Figure 2A-3's note reiterates that lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder or 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, with lower minimums per Section 2A.16. - [Image 3] Figure 2M-3 shows the same rural offset conventions (12 ft MIN. from the traveled way, 6 ft MIN. from a paved shoulder, 5 ft MIN. height) applied to recreational-area sign assemblies, consistent with Figure 2A-2. Citations: - Section 2A.15 Standard §4 (p.58) - Section 2A.15 Standard §5 (p.58) - Section 2A.13 Guidance §6 (p.57) - Section 2A.16 Option §9 (p.60) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Page 92 - Page 93 - Page 100 - Page 566
gold_answer: The minimum mounting height is 5 feet. The normal minimum lateral offset is 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, or 6 feet from the edge of a shoulder wider than 6 feet.
